mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w is a leading indicator of weaker weekday discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks. If workplace mobility stays depressed, retail visits should soften with a short lag.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -2.4 at t-2w to -13.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below -8 for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not end below its last-28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated and WORKPLACES weakens at the same time, people substitute from commuting to at-home activity and reduce discretionary retail trips within two weeks. The recent rise in RESIDENTIAL combined with the workplace drop implies a downward retail signal.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 10 while WORKPLACES is below -10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 11.7 at t-0w while WORKPLACES fell to -13.1
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and WORKPLACES stays below -10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A positive breakout in PARKS signals improved outdoor circulation and social outings, which then spills over into nearby retail and recreation demand over the next four weeks. The t-0w jump in PARKS should therefore predict higher RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -6.7 at t-1w to 1.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains positive for two consecutive weeks after crossing above zero but RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in TRANSIT below its recent range indicates weaker public movement and more cautious trip-making, which suppresses retail visits over the next one to two weeks. The recent worsening in TRANSIT should therefore precede lower RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell to -14.0 at t-0w after -11.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -12 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM softens while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, errands are being consolidated at home or locally, which reduces discretionary retail outings over the next four weeks. The combination should predict a lower RETAIL_REC trend even if grocery declines are modest.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed negative while RESIDENTIAL stayed above 8 in all weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 and GROCERY_PHARM stays below 0 for four weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rise in PARKS can precede higher retail demand only when WORKPLACES is not simultaneously falling, because outdoor leisure then acts as a general mobility booster rather than a substitute for shopping. In that regime, RETAIL_REC should improve within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0 and WORKPLACES stays above -5
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS crossed above 0 at t-0w while WORKPLACES fell sharply negative
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above 0 while WORKPLACES stays above -5 for a week and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising GROCERY_PHARM and rising PARKS indicates broader local movement and trip chaining, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks. This effect should appear only when both series are moving upward together.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both increase for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -5.7 to -3.6 while PARKS improved from -12.9 to 1.7
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS rise for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior 28-day average within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A near-term transit slump followed by workplace weakness indicates a broader demand shock that transmits to retail with a four-week lag. Because TRANSIT is already very low and WORKPLACES turned sharply negative at t-0w, RETAIL_REC should be lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -12 and WORKPLACES below -10 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -14.0 and WORKPLACES is -13.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both below -10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC is not below its last-28-day mean after 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
